newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso pares gains but firm on quiet election.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso pares gains but firm on quiet election.

text.p: The Mexican peso moderated some of its earlier advances at the close on Monday due to forecast falls in domestic interest rates and profit-taking.
Still, the peso ended firm after dealers shed long dollar positions in the wake of relatively smooth mid-term elections, dealers said.
"The important thing is there were no disturbances," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate ended the day 2.2 and 2.3 centavos firmer, respectively, at 7.9210/7.9250 and 7.9180/7.9220 per dollar.
"Otherwise, it was to be expected that Cardenas should win," the dealer added.

Mexicans voted on Sunday to replace the lower chamber of Congress, a quarter of the Senate and six state governors and, for the first time in modern Mexico, to elect a mayor of Mexico City. The post had been previously occupied by a presidential nominee.

Cuauhtemoc Cardenas, of the left-wing Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD) had a commanding lead with returns counted from 86 percent of polling booths in the capital. President Zedillo had already congratulated Cardenas on Sunday.
Dealers said the peso softened in late trade amid market forecasts bellwether 28-day Cetes rates could fall by up to 200 basis points at Tuesday night's primary auction.
"We have to watch that real (interest) rates don't fall to far, because that could put the peso under some pressure," one dealer said.

"People who had sold long dollar positions this morning put the peso under some pressure this afternoon," another dealer said. "Furthermore, some went short and when that didn't work, they bought back dollars," he added.
Same-day peso contracts had earlier closed dealing 3.4 centavos firmer at 7.8970/7.8990 per dollar.
